UC San Diego Health is proud to be a four-time Magnet-designated organization and has now earned Magnet with Distinction from the American Nurses Credentialing Center (ANCC). Magnet is the gold standard for nursing excellence, achieved by only about 10% of hospitals worldwide. Magnet with Distinction is awarded to the highest-performing Magnet organizations, with only a select few earning this prestigious honor. This recognition reflects our commitment to transformational leadership, professional nursing excellence, innovation, exceptional patient outcomes, and an empowering practice environment where nurses thrive.

The UC San Diego Alpha Clinic is the cell and gene therapy arm of the Sanford Stem Cell Clinical Center and specializes in early-phase, first-in-human trials. The Sanford Stem Cell Clinical Center is devoted to accelerating the translation of all types of stem cell research to safe and effective therapies. It attracts patients, funding agencies, and study sponsors to participate in, support, and accelerate novel stem cell clinical trials and ancillary studies for a range of difficult diseases. The Sanford Stem Cell Clinical Center has expanded to become one of six centers under the Sanford Stem Cell Institute umbrella.

Under general supervision, the Senior LVN is responsible for performing a wide range of patient care activities. Duties include, but are not limited to, prioritizing and assisting with patient phone calls, administering medications, collecting data, performing procedures, obtaining specimens, providing patient and family education, and reviewing treatment plans.

The Senior LVN also performs clinical study–related procedures in accordance with study protocols for patients participating in clinical trials. These duties may include central venous access, blood draws, dressing changes, peripheral blood draws, peripheral IV insertion, hydration, injections, procedure assistance, EKGs, vital signs, and rooming patients. In addition to clinical trial–related procedures, the Senior LVN also provides support for standard-of-care patient visits as part of routine clinic operations.

The Senior LVN serves as a liaison between physicians and patients, as well as a patient educator. Other related duties may be assigned as needed. All job standards are expected to be performed at an expert level.
Proficiency in nursing procedures, specimen collection, specimen handling, and specimen testing, as applicable to assigned duties.
Demonstrated knowledge and skills in performing basic nursing techniques and procedures, including venipuncture and patient blood specimen collection.
Knowledge of universal precautions, infection prevention and control, and proper body mechanics.

Strong organizational skills with demonstrated ability to prioritize assignments, manage workflow, and work productively in meeting critical deadlines with constantly changing priorities and interruptions.
Ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive patient information appropriately.
Effective verbal and written communication skills, with the interpersonal skills, tact, and diplomacy necessary to interact professionally with providers, staff, and a diverse patient population.
Demonstrated ability to communicate professionally by telephone and provide appropriate patient-facing service.
